rv.q: In all, Baby is a genial, sweet, entertaining journey into and through one of the most powerful and important things that any couple goes through.
Citadel Theatre’s latest production is warm and winning, despite a book that’s often feels more like a situation comedy than a humorous and thoughtful musical about pregnancy.
The music by David Shire contains few if any notable hooks, and the lyrics by Richard Maltby, Jr. are cheesy and gauche.
"Baby" the Musical had a deep hold on me.
Combine perfect casting with the keen insight of director Scott Shallenbarger and you have the superb production of 'Baby,' now on stage at Citadel Theatre in Lake Forest.

cn.t: This charming but modest 1980s musical about three couples facing pregnancy receives warm praise for its perfect casting and strong direction, though critics note its purposefully diverse characters feel schematic and the show lacks the spark to be truly memorable.
